question: At 55 mph, what advance placement distances does Table 2C-3 show for Condition A and for a potential stop condition?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For a posted or 85th-percentile speed of 55 mph, Table 2C-3 shows an advance placement distance of 990 feet for Condition A (speed reduction and lane changing in heavy traffic). For a potential stop condition — which is the Condition B "0 mph" column, typical of Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead, Signal Ahead, and Intersection Warning signs — the table shows 495 feet. Guidance (recommended): - The Table 2C-3 row for 55 mph reads: "55 mph 990 ft 495 ft 275 ft 225 ft 200 ft 125 ft N/A5," where 990 ft is the Condition A distance and 495 ft is the Condition B distance for deceleration to 0 mph (the potential stop condition). - Per the table's footnote 1, "The distances are adjusted for a sign legibility distance of 180 feet for Condition A. The distances for Condition B (with the exception of the potential stop condition) have been adjusted for a sign legibility distance of 250 feet... For Conditions A and B, warning signs with less than 6-inch legend or more than four words, a minimum of 100 feet should be added to the advance placement distance." - The distances in Table 2C-3 should be applied with engineering judgment as an aid for determining warning sign location. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2C-3, where the 55 mph row lists 990 ft under Condition A and 495 ft under the Condition B "0³" (potential stop) column; footnote 3 identifies the 0-mph column as "the warning of a potential stop situation... based on the 2018 AASHTO Policy, Table 3-1, Stopping Sight Distance, providing a PRT of 2.5 seconds, a deceleration rate of 11.2 feet/second²." [Image 2] shows the same table in context of Section 2C.04, Placement of Warning Signs, confirming the 55 mph row values of 990 ft (Condition A) and 495 ft (Condition B, 0 mph). Citations: - Table 2C-3 (p.152) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §804 (p.153) - Section 2C.04 Guidance §5 (p.152)
gold_answer: 990 feet for Condition A and 495 feet for the potential stop condition.
